title: Characterizing globally linked pairs in graphs
summary: A pair $\{u,v\}$ of vertices is said to be globally linked in a $d$-dimensional framework $(G,p)$ if there exists no other framework $(G,q)$ with the same edge lengths, in which the distance between the points corresponding to $u$ and $v$ is different from that in $(G,p)$. We say that $\{u,v\}$ is globally linked in $G$ in $\R^d$ if $\{u,v\}$ is globally linked in every generic $d$-dimensional framework $(G,p)$.
